_comment: Guided tour of step 1 (Data Selection) of the native Burst Analysis workflow. Targets are item_rects keys of BurstDataSelectionApp; the action steps wait for the control.

steps.title: What the workflow works on
steps.text: Every later step reads the files of this step. Each has a role: the measurements are searched for bursts; the buffer, an IRF and a reference dye per colour calibrate.

steps.title: The workspace's data
steps.text: The photon streams in the Datasets workspace. A group of files dropped together is one row. Drop files on the ChiSurf window to add more.

steps.title: Drag each dataset onto its role
steps.text: One row per role, made from the setup of step 0: Measurement, Buffer, and per colour an IRF and a Reference dye. Drag a workspace row onto the role it is; the row under the pointer lights up. Right-click › Move to changes it later.

await.hint: Drag a workspace row onto a role row (or right-click it › Add to).

steps.title: The reference dye
steps.text: Its Dye cell picks the dye from the dye database — found in the file's header or name, else the colour's usual dye. Its D gives the confocal volume; its decays give the G factor.

steps.title: What is estimated instead
steps.text: No row but Measurement is needed. Missing ones are said here: the background and IRF are then estimated from the measurement and G is taken from the setup.

steps.title: The calibration (Advanced)
steps.text: The buffer's background rates, each colour's G factor beside the setup's with Apply G to the setup, the temperature D is corrected to, and the confocal volume with its fitted correlation. In Simple mode G is applied as it is computed.

steps.title: Go on
steps.text: The burst search (step 2) gets the measurements and the detector setup of step 0; Burst MLE gets the IRF and buffer.
